defects.rationale: The default list is shared across all calls, so tags accumulate between invocations instead of starting empty.

issues.observation: The review reports exactly one finding (a mutable default argument). A single finding is a strong signal the pass stopped at the first easy issue; typical review snippets of this kind also contain at least one other material defect (e.g., unvalidated input, unchecked return, resource not closed, or an interaction with the shared default list such as it being mutated and then returned to the caller).

Line 1 is cited for the mutable default. That is plausible only if the function signature occupies line 1; the rationale does not quote or name the parameter, so the evidence link between the cited line and the defect cannot be confirmed.
The rationale states accumulation across calls but does not describe the concrete failure path (which call site observes the stale tags, and what incorrect data results).

revision_instructions: Re-scan the entire supplied snippet line by line and add every additional material defect you can support with a specific line, up to the eight-finding limit; do not stop after the mutable-default finding.
In the mutable-default rationale, name the specific parameter and the line's exact operation so the cited line is verifiably the source of the defect.
Extend each rationale to describe the concrete failure path (what wrong value or error a subsequent caller observes), not just the general category of risk.
Do not alter the existing mutable_default finding's category or line if they are correct; only enrich its rationale.
